web.description:
Search

- [measure between -23dB and -18dB RMS](https://www.acx.com/help/acx-audio-submission-requirements/201456300#RMS) and [have -3dB peak values](https://www.acx.com/help/acx-audio-submission-requirements/201456300#Peak-levels) and

- [be a 192kbps or higher MP3, Constant Bit Rate (CBR)](https://www.acx.com/help/acx-audio-submission-requirements/201456300#192kbps-MP3) at [44.1 kHz](https://www.acx.com/help/acx-audio-submission-requirements/201456300#44.1-kHz)

Basically, if your RMS is between -18dB and -23dB RMS, with peaks at -3dB, you’ll achieve the optimal sound across all formats.

For example, a production with a low RMS but loud peaks could end up with technical issues within the file, such as uneven narration levels, a high noise floor, etc.

**A:** Peaks are the loudest part or parts of an audio file.

This lets you bring up the overall volume of your audio, which may be necessary to meet ACX’s RMS requirement (-18dB RMS to -23dB RMS).

Since ACX’s peaks requirement is -3dB, you can now raise the overall level of the audio by +4dB.

web.description:
# Meeting ACX Standards: How Studio 713 Ensures Compliance
### **Understanding ACX Technical Requirements**
- **Loudness Levels**: Each file should have an RMS between -23dB and -18dB, with peak values no higher than -3dB.

### **Studio 713’s Approach to ACX Compliance**
- **Post-Production Excellence**: We handle editing, mixing, and mastering, adjusting levels to meet RMS and peak requirements, and applying noise reduction techniques to achieve the required noise floor.
